Home/Teacher: Lab Forms + Canvas

Lab Forms + Canvas

Every reflection question in the lessons (socratic checkpoints and bug hunts, where a lesson keeps one) has an answer box, injected at build time bysrc/lib/formify.ts. Answers save on the student's device as they type, and each lesson has aDownload answers (.json) button that produces one small, self-describing file — the question text, the student's answer, and a stable question id (like 4.5:sc1:q2) all travel together. This page is the whole loop for collecting and returning them through Canvas.

1. What students do

  1. Open the lesson (e.g. 1.4).
  2. Type their name in the bar at the bottom of the lesson once — it is remembered on that device for every other lesson.
  3. Answer the boxed questions as they work through the labs. Everything autosaves locally; nothing is lost if they close the tab.
  4. Click Download answers (.json) and upload that file to the Canvas assignment.

The Dashboard also has a My work panel: one file backs up all answers plus progress, and can be restored on another machine (useful when lab machines get reimaged).

2. Set up the Canvas assignment (once per lesson)

  1. In Canvas: Assignments → + Assignment.
  2. Submission Type: Online, checkFile Uploads. (Leave "Allowed File Types" blank so .json files upload cleanly.)
  3. Set points and the due date, then Publish.

3. Read the submissions

Each submitted file is plain JSON you can open in any text editor, a browser, or cat. It looks like this:

{
  "format": "apcsp-lab-answers/1",
  "student": "Ada Lovelace",
  "lesson": "4.5",
  "lessonTitle": "The Full State Machine: Patrol, Chase, Attack",
  "downloadedAt": "2026-11-17T16:02:11.402Z",
  "answers": [
    {
      "id": "4.5:bh1:q1",
      "block": "bug-hunt",
      "question": "The enemy jitters because the flip condition...",
      "answer": "..."
    },
    {
      "id": "4.5:sc1:q1",
      "block": "socratic",
      "question": "Falling out of the chase if means it returns...",
      "answer": "..."
    }
  ]
}

Because the question text rides along in the file, you can grade from the JSON alone — no need to open the site side by side. The id tells you the lesson, the block (bh = bug hunt, sc = socratic, dc = the Break It Down discussion), and the question number.

4. Return feedback

  1. In the Canvas gradebook: SpeedGrader shows the .json as an attachment; open it in a new tab and read.
  2. Type the score and one line of feedback — the boxes are worth a few completion points, not essays; the labs themselves are where the learning shows.
  3. For a whole-class snapshot, Download Submissionson the assignment page and skim the files.
The MCQ clinic sets grade themselves. The three exam clinics (11.4a/b/c) now ship 48 real questions rendered fromsrc/data/mcq-bank.ts. Students answer on the page, pressGrade this set, and get a score plus the per-family error table the lesson asks them to build by hand. Those letters ride into the same answers .json you already collect — each question carries a hidden answer field, so no separate collection step is needed.

Reflective answer boxes are still hand-graded: they are worth a few completion points, and the labs are where the learning shows. Only the MCQ sets are objective, and only they are autoscored.

5. MCQ bank — what to change and what it guards

To do thisEdit
Add or reword a questionsrc/data/mcq-bank.ts — the three clinic lessons, the key below, and /data/mcq-keys.json all regenerate from it
Reorder a setDo not. Question ids are positional (11.4a:mc:q3), so reordering re-points students' saved answers and the keys' letter grades at the wrong question. Append, or rewrite a question in place
Change an answeranswer: is a 0-based index into choices — 0 is A
Check nothing driftednpm run verify — check 6 fails if any key lacks a rendered question, any explanation is missing, any CED family is unknown, or the mixed sets fall outside the exam's big-idea ranges

Published weighting vs. what the sets actually contain

Sets 1 and 3 are the mixed practice sets and are held to the exam's published big-idea ranges. Set 2 is the targeted data-and-networks remediation set, so it deliberately spikes BI2 and BI4 and isexcluded from that assertion — compare the two columns below and the reason is visible.

6. Answer key (48 questions)

The same key the page grader fetches, printed here so you can see it at a glance while grading or reviewing a set in class. Generated fromsrc/data/mcq-bank.ts at build time — never edit this table by hand.

Rationales for every question are in the answers.json that ships to students and insrc/data/mcq-bank.ts itself; the grader reveals each one on screen when a student presses Grade this set.

7. The Create PT exception

College Board collaboration rules apply during the Create PT build days (April 13-27). Answer boxes on those lessons stay usable forstandup notes, but the graded artifact is the program itself submitted to the AP Digital Portfolio, not Canvas. Keep Canvas for the process grade (commits, gates hit) and the exam clinics.

Site maintenance cheat-sheet

To do thisRun / edit this
Add or re-date a lessonsrc/data/curriculum.ts (SEQUENCE) — the dashboard, chain, pace table, and PACING.md all follow automatically
Rename a lesson titlesrc/data/lessons.ts + the lesson page's h1
Scaffold a new lesson pagenpm run new-lesson -- 5.11
Check site integritynpm run build && npm run verify
Re-generate PACING.md / sitemaphappens inside every npm run build
Search indexPagefind runs in build; nothing to maintain
Add / reword an MCQsrc/data/mcq-bank.ts — lessons, key page, and /data/mcq-keys.json all regenerate. Never reorder a set (ids are positional)
